chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya and Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from Abdullah ibn Ja'far, from Ahmad ibn Hamza, who said:

I said to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him): A man from your mawla has relatives, all of whom believe in you, and he has zakat. Is it permissible for him to give them all of his zakat? He (peace be upon him) said: Yes.
ai.seo_question: Can a person give all of their zakat to their believing relatives?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that a single relative can receive the entirety of one's zakat, resolving the common concern that distribution must be split among multiple recipients. It underscores the Shia principle of prioritizing kinship (qaraba) within the community of believers, specifically linking eligibility to faith in the Imam. This ruling facilitates strengthening family ties and supporting dependents without the administrative burden of dividing the amount among many individuals.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, and Muhammad Bin Abdullah, from Abdullah Bin Ja’far, from Ahmad Bin Hamza who said,

‘I said to Abu Al-Hassanasws, ‘A man from the ones in yourasws Wilayah has relatives for him, all of them are saying (believing) in youasws, and for him is Zakāt (to be given out). Is it allowed for him that he gives them the entirety of his Zakāt?’ Heasws said: ‘Yes’.
en.sarwar: 7. Muhammad ibn Yahya and Muhammad ibn ‘Abd Allah have narrated from ‘Abd Allah ibn Ja‘far from Ahmad ibn Hamzah who has said the following:

“I once asked abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who is one of your followers whose relatives all speak of you and he owes Zakat; can he pay all of his Zakat to them. He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, he can do so.’”
